expected_evidence: geological: elevated nanodiamond (cubic/lonsdaleite) concentrations in a discrete stratigraphic layer (the 'black mat'/Younger Dryas boundary layer) across multiple North American sedimentary sequences dated to ~12,900 cal BP
geological: associated platinum, iridium, or other siderophile-element anomalies, magnetic spherules, and glassy/melted microspherules in the same boundary layer
geological: charcoal and soot spikes indicating continent-wide biomass burning coincident with the layer
material/archaeological: disruption or abandonment signatures at Clovis-age sites directly above/below the boundary layer
material: absence of a confirmed impact crater (expected under an airburst-only mechanism, so its absence is not disconfirming)
astronomical: theoretical/modeling evidence of an airburst event (fragmentation of a comet/bolide), though no direct instrumental record is possible for this era
genetic: megafaunal extinction bottleneck signals and/or human population genetic discontinuity around 12.9 ka in North America
oral_tradition: indigenous narratives referencing fire-from-sky, darkness, or catastrophic events that could be post-hoc associated with the event
iconographic: rock art or petroglyph motifs proposed (controversially) to depict a cosmic/airburst event
response.rationale: This hypothesis corresponds to the well-known Younger Dryas Impact Hypothesis (YDIH), placing the nanodiamond/impact-proxy signature at ~10,950 BCE in North America. Using the 'younger-dryas' row, the most relevant evidence channels are geological (0.65) and material (0.35), which are the actual channels this hypothesis rests on (sediment stratigraphy, nanodiamonds, spherules, platinum anomalies, charcoal layers) — both are moderately-to-well detectable, meaning the evidence class is not intrinsically hidden from discovery. Astronomical detectability is nominally high (0.7) but is not really applicable here since no direct instrumental record of a prehistoric airburst can exist; the absence of a crater is expected, not diagnostic, under an airburst mechanism. Genetic (0.3), oral_tradition (0.1), and iconographic (0.1) channels are weak and speculative corroborators at best. Because geological/material detectability is moderate-to-good and this is precisely the kind of evidence that has, in fact, been reported at multiple North American sites (Firestone et al. and follow-on studies), the hypothesis could plausibly have left detectable traces and such traces have plausibly been found — this is a live, actively debated empirical claim in the literature rather than a case explained by low detectability. However, replication of nanodiamond/spherule signals has been inconsistent across independent labs (a known point of contention I recall as model-prior, not verified from provided evidence text), so the primary uncertainty here is about interpretive/methodological reliability and reproducibility of the corroborating data, not about whether evidence could physically survive/be observed. I set the aggregate detectability adjustment at 0.55, reflecting a mix dominated by the higher geological/material channels but tempered by the near-zero contribution of textual, linguistic, and iconographic channels for this period.
